title: Example 18-13: Diagramming with Multiple Arrow Shafts

illustrates.quote:
Spatial Diagrams with Arrows and Multiple Shafts
a. Place the appropriate symbol of the arrow above the first letter of the word to which the arrow points. (See UEB, §3.2.)
b. Use line mode to represent the arrow shaft. The line should end above the first letter of the word from which the arrow points. (See UEB, §16.2.3, Horizontal Line Mode.)

blocks.text: A branching line above the sentence: a downward arrowhead points to "crowd", and two line-mode shafts drop from it to "large" and "friendly" (both italicized). Not modeled: F-189.

print.printFeatures: The words 'large' and 'friendly' are italicized; an arrow diagram is drawn above the text.
